projects.title: DocPulseAI - Code Intelligence & Living Documentation
projects.summary: Built an AI-driven platform that keeps architecture docs synced with source code using AST analysis and CI workflows.
projects.description: DocPulseAI extracts API/entity/dependency metadata from repositories, generates architecture documentation and diagrams, and flags documentation drift.
projects.focus: AST code intelligence, living documentation, CI-based updates
projects.problem: Teams lose time when architecture docs become stale and system dependencies are not visible from code alone.
goals: Extract APIs, entities, and service relationships directly from source code.
Generate living documentation and architecture diagrams automatically.
Integrate documentation refresh into CI workflows.
ownership: Implemented Tree-sitter powered analysis pipelines for repository scanning.
Designed backend services for metadata extraction and document generation.
Built dashboard flows for documentation health and repository impact insights.
constraints: Needed consistent results across mixed coding styles and project structures.
Had to balance extraction depth with practical execution time.
architecture: Tree-sitter based analysis engine parses repositories into structured metadata.
Documentation and drift-detection services generate and validate living docs.
React dashboard visualizes architecture insights and change summaries.
qualitySignals: AST-based extraction reduced manual documentation drift.
Modular service boundaries kept analysis and rendering concerns separated.
CI-oriented flow enabled repeatable and automated updates.
impact: Reduced manual effort required to maintain technical documentation.
Improved onboarding clarity for unfamiliar repositories.
Made architecture insights directly queryable and reviewable.
challenges: Normalizing extracted signals across repositories with varying conventions.
Presenting technical findings in a way that remains useful for daily development.
nextSteps: Extend multi-language analyzers for broader repository coverage.
Improve ranking and relevance scoring for dependency exploration.

projects.title: Edge Co-Intelligence System
projects.summary: Designed a distributed YOLOv8 inference platform with worker heartbeats, weighted load balancing, and retry-aware failover.
projects.description: The system dispatches frames to edge workers, streams annotated output in real time, and provides Angular dashboards for operations and admin analytics.
projects.focus: Distributed inference orchestration, real-time streaming, fault tolerance
projects.problem: Single-node inference became a bottleneck and failure hotspot under high-throughput workloads.
goals: Parallelize inference across worker nodes.
Maintain low latency while scaling throughput.
Recover gracefully from worker instability.
ownership: Built coordinator services for worker registration, heartbeat, and queue orchestration.
Implemented retry queues, circuit-breaker behavior, and health-aware dispatching.
Integrated real-time stream outputs and dashboard-facing metrics/summary APIs.
constraints: Worker availability and processing capacity changed over time.
Ordering and consistency had to be preserved while handling retries.
architecture: FastAPI coordinator dispatches frames to edge worker agents for parallel YOLO inference.
Results pipeline aggregates detections and streams annotated MJPEG output.
Separate admin backend + Angular portal track cameras, analytics, and control commands.
qualitySignals: Health-aware scheduling reduced avoidable failures.
Failover and retry paths improved stability under churn.
Distributed design removed single-node bottlenecks.
impact: Increased effective inference throughput.
Improved resiliency during worker failures.
Enabled steadier real-time response behavior.
challenges: Balancing throughput, latency, and consistency simultaneously.
Avoiding duplicate or dropped results during failover.
nextSteps: Add autoscaling policies based on queue depth and latency.
Expose observability dashboards for worker-level diagnostics.

projects.title: Quizora - AI-Assisted Online Quiz Platform
projects.summary: Built an AI-assisted quiz platform with faculty/student role separation, secure code-based access, and auto-evaluation.
projects.description: Quizora enables faculty to generate questions from syllabus content, edit/publish assessments, and analyze attempts while students access quizzes via unique codes.
projects.focus: AI-assisted quiz generation, secure role workflows, assessment automation
projects.problem: Traditional quiz systems are slow to author, hard to scale, and often weak on role-based access control.
goals: Enable faculty to generate/edit quiz content quickly with AI support.
Provide secure faculty and student workflows.
Automate scoring and performance analytics.
ownership: Implemented Spring Boot APIs for quiz authoring, publishing, attempts, and results.
Integrated Spring AI based question generation from uploaded syllabus/PDF content.
Built security flows with JWT auth, OTP-based verification, and role-based access control.
constraints: AI-generated output needed faculty oversight before publishing.
Assessment flows required strict access boundaries by role.
architecture: Spring Boot services manage quiz lifecycle and evaluation workflows.
React frontend provides distinct faculty and student surfaces.
MySQL persistence stores users, quizzes, attempts, and analytics entities.
qualitySignals: Role-isolated workflows reduced unauthorized operations.
Automated scoring reduced grading turnaround time.
AI-assisted authoring improved quiz creation speed.
impact: Improved faculty productivity for assessment creation.
Delivered secure and simpler student quiz access with unique codes.
Provided analytics-ready data for performance review.
challenges: Maintaining reliable quiz integrity across authoring and publishing stages.
Ensuring generated questions stay academically relevant.
nextSteps: Add deeper performance analytics across topic clusters.
Expand question quality checks and review tooling.

projects.title: SaatDin - Parametric Income Insurance for Riders
projects.summary: Built an Android-first parametric insurance platform that auto-triggers payouts for delivery riders when disruption thresholds are hit.
projects.description: SaatDin protects weekly income for Q-commerce riders by monitoring weather, AQI, and traffic signals at pincode level and issuing automated payouts without manual claims.
projects.focus: Parametric insurance, risk decisioning, mobile-first operations
projects.problem: Delivery riders lose daily earnings during severe rain, poor air quality, and heavy traffic events, with no reliable short-cycle safety net.
goals: Build a mobile-first insurance flow tailored for delivery riders.
Automate trigger detection and payout decisions at pincode granularity.
Keep decisions auditable with fallback escalation paths.
ownership: Designed triage decisioning across rules, ML, and LLM-assisted reasoning.
Implemented backend workflows for monitoring, trigger evaluation, and payout flow.
Integrated rider-focused onboarding and policy interactions in Flutter app flow.
constraints: Needed precise zone-level trigger logic to avoid broad false payouts.
Had to keep interaction latency low for on-shift riders using only mobile devices.
architecture: FastAPI backend orchestrates policy, trigger, and payout workflows.
TriBrain decision engine (LangGraph): rules -> ML -> LLM fallback routing.
Flutter mobile client delivers onboarding, coverage, and payout status flows.
qualitySignals: Pincode-scoped trigger evaluation improved payout precision.
Tiered decisioning improved reliability with explainable routing.
Automated path reduced claim friction for riders.
impact: Converted income-protection concept into an implementable product flow.
Improved trust by reducing manual claim dependency.
Demonstrated practical fusion of rules, ML, and LLM orchestration.
challenges: Balancing fast automated payouts with false-positive risk control.
Designing clear policy boundaries and exclusions for real-world use.
nextSteps: Expand trigger coverage with more reliable mobility and civic data feeds.
Strengthen simulation and backtesting for policy threshold tuning.

projects.title: SnapDish - Multi-Role Food Delivery Platform
projects.summary: Built a full-stack food delivery ecosystem with separate apps for customers, restaurants, delivery agents, and platform admins.
projects.description: SnapDish combines ordering, operations, and delivery into one MERN platform with role-specific frontends and a centralized backend for lifecycle and analytics flows.
projects.focus: Order lifecycle reliability, role-based workflows, operational analytics
projects.problem: Food delivery operations break down when order states, partner actions, and platform oversight are not coordinated in a single reliable workflow.
goals: Implement clear end-to-end order states from checkout to delivery.
Support all platform actors with role-specific products.
Provide admin and restaurant insights with reporting dashboards.
ownership: Implemented backend APIs for menus, carts, orders, and partner operations.
Connected four client apps to a common auth and order workflow.
Built analytics/reporting surfaces for admin and operational monitoring.
constraints: Order transitions had to remain consistent under concurrent updates.
Dashboards required efficient querying across high-volume operational data.
architecture: Node.js + Express backend exposes role-aware REST endpoints.
MongoDB stores user, restaurant, order, and transaction domain data.
Separate frontend apps: customer, restaurant-admin, delivery-agent, and main admin.
qualitySignals: Role-specific app boundaries improved workflow clarity.
Central order-state model reduced fulfillment ambiguity.
Analytics-oriented endpoints improved operational visibility.
impact: Enabled coordinated multi-actor delivery operations.
Improved traceability of order progress and exceptions.
Created a scalable base for future logistics and commerce enhancements.
challenges: Synchronizing status updates across customer, restaurant, and rider views.
Balancing transaction-heavy APIs with dashboard read performance.
nextSteps: Add event-driven notifications for all critical state transitions.
Introduce caching for high-frequency admin and restaurant analytics.

projects.title: Air Quality Prediction Platform
projects.summary: Built an end-to-end AQI prediction app with Flask model serving, React frontend, and OpenWeather integration.
projects.description: The project combines training notebooks and a production-style inference API to deliver city-level AQI prediction through a web interface.
projects.focus: Model serving, feature engineering, full-stack ML delivery
projects.problem: AQI forecasting requires combining noisy pollutant signals with practical serving architecture for real usage.
goals: Train and evaluate AQI prediction models using pollutant features.
Expose prediction results through an API-backed application.
Provide a user-facing interface for real-time AQI insights.
ownership: Prepared and evaluated models in Jupyter notebooks using pollutant features.
Served RandomForestRegressor inference through a Flask backend.
Built React frontend workflows for real-time AQI prediction requests.
constraints: Prediction quality depended on external API signal consistency.
Model output had to remain understandable for non-ML users.
architecture: Notebook pipeline trains and validates a RandomForestRegressor (500 estimators).
Flask API performs inference via persisted model artifacts.
React frontend consumes API responses and renders AQI prediction details.
qualitySignals: 8-feature pollutant model design improved prediction consistency.
Separation of training and serving improved maintainability.
Docker-based setup supported reproducible local deployment.
impact: Delivered practical AQI prediction in an accessible web interface.
Connected ML experimentation to a usable application workflow.
Created a foundation for city-level trend and historical analysis.
challenges: Stabilizing prediction quality across changing environmental signals.
Bridging notebook experimentation with production-style API serving.
nextSteps: Add historical trend visualizations and batch predictions.
Introduce scheduled retraining and drift monitoring.

projects.title: Mobile Network Simulation System
projects.summary: Built a graph-based cellular network simulator with dynamic tower handover, call routing, and multi-network switching.
projects.description: A Python simulation that models network zones, towers, users, movement, and call behavior with explicit handling for out-of-coverage scenarios.
projects.focus: Network simulation, routing logic, mobility modeling
projects.problem: Understanding tower handover and call routing behavior is difficult without a controllable simulation environment.
goals: Model network zones with tower coverage and user mobility.
Simulate automatic handover as users move between coverage areas.
Route calls through towers and switching centers with error handling.
ownership: Implemented simulation flow and interactive CLI controls.
Built movement and nearest-tower selection logic for connectivity.
Added call-path and network-switching capabilities.
constraints: Coverage behavior needed deterministic rules for reproducible outcomes.
Simulation had to handle disconnected users gracefully.
architecture: Graph-style network representation connects towers and network zones.
Runtime engine tracks users, movement events, and connection state.
Call orchestration models pathing through connected network components.
qualitySignals: Structured simulation entities improved maintainability.
Input validation and explicit failure states reduced runtime ambiguity.
Clear handover logic made mobility behavior easier to inspect.
impact: Created an educational testbed for telecom-style behavior.
Made network handover and routing dynamics observable.
Demonstrated practical systems thinking around state transitions.
challenges: Coordinating user movement with connection consistency.
Preserving call reliability across dynamic connectivity changes.
nextSteps: Add visualization for tower coverage and active call paths.
Introduce simulation metrics (handover rate, dropped-call rate).

projects.title: Banking Transaction API
projects.summary: Built a Spring Boot banking backend for account operations, deposits, withdrawals, transfers, and transaction history.
projects.description: A Java backend service using Spring Data JPA for account and transaction management, with PostgreSQL persistence and REST APIs for core banking flows.
projects.focus: Transactional API design, account lifecycle, data persistence
projects.problem: Core banking workflows require reliable account state updates and auditable transaction flows.
goals: Implement account CRUD and account-type updates through REST endpoints.
Support deposit, withdrawal, and account-to-account transfer operations.
Provide account-based transaction retrieval for history and auditing.
ownership: Implemented account and transaction controllers for banking operations.
Built service-layer logic for balance updates and transfer bookkeeping.
Integrated JPA repositories for account and transaction persistence.
constraints: Balance validation was required to prevent invalid withdrawals/transfers.
Transaction history needed to stay linked to account identifiers.
architecture: Spring Boot REST API with controller-service-repository layering.
Spring Data JPA repositories manage Account and Transaction entities.
PostgreSQL-backed persistence configured through application properties.
qualitySignals: Clear service-layer separation improved maintainability.
Validation checks enforce amount and balance safety rules.
Transfer flow writes debit/credit records for both accounts.
impact: Delivered complete baseline banking transaction workflows.
Created reusable backend patterns for financial operations projects.
Improved practical experience with Java API and persistence design.
challenges: Keeping account balance updates consistent across operation types.
Designing concise API responses for both success and error paths.
nextSteps: Add authentication/authorization enforcement for protected routes.
Introduce stronger transaction consistency controls and test coverage.
